page: Microsoft Azure E16-4ds_v5 is an EDSv5-family virtual machine configured with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled, providing 614 GB of temporary disk capacity with Premium Storage capability, managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear tradeoff between single-core capabilities and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core execution, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, falls within the average range. However, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, register in the bottom 25% due to the low physical core count. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached large blocks also perform in the lower quartile, though Passmark memory scores remain average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server type provides a dense memory footprint and local storage without requiring a high vCPU count, making it suitable for workloads that are memory-intensive but compute-light. It is well-suited for hosting small to medium databases, caching layers, and memory-bound enterprise applications that do not require massive parallel processing power.
